Vaultless storage of credentials

AuthNull Enables Vaultless storage of credentials

AuthNull helps enables you to store vaults in a decentralized wallet, owned by the user and managed by two roots of trust.

Decentralized Authenticator Wallet

AuthNull's Authenticator Wallet also serves as a credential storage for recieving all credentials - passwordless credentials, as well as SSH Keys and passwords.

Automated distribution and lookups

When enabled, SSH Keys and Passwords (as one of the factors) are automatically rotated and distributed to the right wallet users who currently have the privileges to the same.

Automated storage / retrieval of Credentials for connected endpoints during authentication.

AuthNull automatically sends credentials - passwordless, passwords, SSH keys, VNC passords, LDAP passwords or SSH Keys automatically to assigned users.

Wallet based credential storage

Tap into your employees' devices to issue and manage credentials decentrally and at scale. This removes a major attack vector for your organization.

When SSH Keys and passwords are rotated by targeted endpoints, the wallets which have pre-existing credentials will automatically receive the updated credentials.

Frequently
asked questions

Answers to the most frequently asked questions.

Users are issued a decentralized wallet when they are onboarded to organizations. This is done after verifying identity. Then either Just in time, or when credential rotation is scheduled, credentials are shared to client wallets. They are not stored in any vault, and during authentication the wallet is pinged to share the wallet credentials.

Let's take the example of an active directory user a@companydomain.com. a@acompanydomain.com is assigned active directory domains - domain1 and domain2. This user will get assigned credentials related to both domains upon onboarding to AuthNull. When the user wants to access a privileged user account say mysql-admin, then when checkedout - mysql-admin credentials are additionally sent to a@companydomain.com's wallet. This could include SSH Keys and / or passwords should that option be enabled as a factor.

If your organization has a credential policy, then all credentials - passwordless credentials, SSH Keys and Passwords are rotated and automatically shipped to respective assigned user's wallets.

Passwordless credentials (also called as Verified credentials - VCs), SSH Keys and Passwords are the kinds of credentials that are stored in the vault.

All credentials issued to users' wallets are automatically revoked when the users are removed from an Identity solution as a part of the Join-Manage-Leave (JML) Lifecycle. Additionally, administrators can force revoke, expire existing wallets as well as credentials.

As a part of the checkout process, previous credentials are expired and new credentials are issued. This means the users who previously held credentials in their vault will see it become inaccessible and the new users will get credential notifications.
